summary.text: 考 is used today to mean “examine,” “test,” or “investigate.” A favored account constructs it from reduced 老, associated with “old” or “elder,” and 丂 as a sound element; the historical uses for “father” and “consider” do not establish how the current meaning developed.

formation.text: The favored analysis is phonosemantic: reduced 老 contributes an “old/elder” category, while 丂 supplies a sound cue. A competing proposal treats 丂 as an earlier graph used for “father,” with 老 added as a classifier. The construction is therefore favored, not settled.

components.text: 耂 is the reduced form of 老 in the favored analysis, with 老’s lower 匕 omitted. It contributes the category “old/elder.”
丂 has a proposed sound role. Its pictured object has been identified variously as a branch, cane or staff, and axe handle; its original name is unsettled.

sound_limitation.text: The shared later readings provide comparisons, but the reported Old Chinese forms differ and were not independently verified; these readings alone do not confirm the ancient sound relation.

sound.text: 丂 and 考 are both recorded with this Middle Chinese transcription; their reported Old Chinese reconstructions differ.
丂 and 考 are both recorded as kǎo in Mandarin; this modern match alone does not establish their ancient sound relation.

history.text: One proposed account says early Western Zhou writing used 老 for both “old” and “father,” then added 丂 to distinguish 考, often omitting the lower 匕 of 老. A competing account proposes that 丂 was used for “father” first and that 老 was added later as a classifier.
The forms change through omission of 老’s lower 匕 in the favored account. 攷 is listed as a variant of 考, but its graphic history and the timing of the two forms’ overlap are unspecified.

uncertainties.text: The pictured object and original name of 丂 remain disputed, so a proposal that its graph was borrowed for “father” because the words sounded alike remains uncertain.
Reported examples use 考 for “father” and “consider/estimate,” and separately for the sounds of 孝 and 巧. They do not date these uses or establish a semantic path to “examine” or “test.”
丂 and 考 share reported Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings but have distinct reported Old Chinese reconstructions; those reconstructions were not independently verified against the inspected table.

senses.text: A traditional lexicographic analysis glosses 考 as “old”; whether this was the graph’s earliest meaning is unresolved.
Reported bronze examples use 考 for “father,” often, though not always, referring to a deceased father.
A reported bronze example uses 考 for “consider” or “estimate”; its date and relation to the “father” use are unresolved.
Current definitions include “examine,” “test,” and “investigate.” Their chronology relative to the reported historical uses is unresolved.

limitations.text: The reported examples and glosses do not establish a chronology or semantic transitions among “old,” “father,” “consider/estimate,” and current “examine/test.”

overview.text: 考 is used for “examine” or “test.” A favored account combines reduced 老, associated with “old/elder,” and 丂 as a sound element. Its reported “father” use does not by itself explain the current meaning.

components.text: 耂 is reduced 老; in the favored account, it contributes the “old/elder” category.

relationships.text: In the favored account, 耂 is reduced 老 and contributes the “old/elder” category; a competing account treats 老 as a classifier added to 丂.

The traditional and favored inscriptional analyses assign 丂 a sound role. Shared Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings are reported, but differing reported Old Chinese forms and uncertainty about 丂 limit what the comparisons establish.
